practiceQuestions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) in the Parliament of India?
opts: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
A member elected specially by the Rajya Sabha from among themselves
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 64 and Article 89(1) of the Constitution of India, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Unlike the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the casting vote of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 100 of the Constitution, all questions at any sitting of either House shall be determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Speaker or person acting as such. The Speaker does not vote in the first instance, but has and shall exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha of independent India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar (G. V. Mavalankar) served as the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha from 1952 to 1956. He is often referred to as the 'Father of the Lok Sabha'.

practiceQuestions.q: Who appoints the 'Pro-Tem Speaker' of the Lok Sabha?
opts: The outgoing Speaker of the Lok Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: The President of India appoints the Pro-Tem Speaker, usually the senior-most member of the Lok Sabha, whose main duty is to administer the oath to the newly elected MPs and preside over the election of the new Speaker.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies certifies a Bill as a Money Bill in the Parliament?
opts: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 110(4) of the Constitution, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the sole and final authority to certify whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not. This decision of the Speaker cannot be questioned in any court.

practiceQuestions.q: By what majority can the Speaker of the Lok Sabha be removed from office?
opts: Simple majority of members present and voting
Absolute majority of the total membership of the House
Two-thirds majority of members present and voting
Two-thirds majority of total membership plus ratification by half of states
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Articles 94 and 96 of the Constitution, the Speaker can be removed by a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by an absolute majority (i.e., a majority of all the then members of the House). Furthermore, 14 days' advance notice must be given of the intention to move such a resolution.

practiceQuestions.q: Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of the Parliament in India?
opts: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 118(4) of the Indian Constitution, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament. If the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker presides, and if the Deputy Speaker is also absent, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides.

practiceQuestions.q: Under which schedule of the Constitution are matters related to disqualification of members on the ground of defection decided by the Presiding Officer?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Tenth Schedule (added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985) contains provisions regarding disqualification of MPs and MLAs on the ground of defection. The presiding officer of the house is the sole authority to decide these cases.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha vote in the first instance during normal legislative proceedings?
opts: Yes, always, because he is a senior constitutional functionary
No, because he is not a member of the Rajya Sabha
Yes, if the Prime Minister permits him to do so
Yes, but only on Money Bills
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) is not a member of the House. Therefore, he does not have a vote in the first instance. He can only exercise a casting vote in the case of a tie (equality of votes).

practiceQuestions.q: Who acts as the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha when the office of the Vice-President is vacant?
opts: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
A person appointed by the Chief Justice of India
The seniormost elected member of the Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: When the office of the Vice-President is vacant, the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are performed by the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Note that the Deputy Chairman performs these duties only as Chairman, and does not assume the office of the President/Vice-President unless elected.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Speaker of the Lok Sabha typically resign from their political party upon election to the office?
opts: It is a mandatory constitutional requirement under Article 93.
To uphold the British convention of political neutrality and absolute impartiality associated with the office.
To prevent being disqualified under the anti-defection law.
To become eligible for appointment as a Union Cabinet Minister later.
practiceQuestions.sol: Although not legally bound by the Indian Constitution to resign from their party (unlike in Britain where the Speaker severs all party ties permanently), Indian Speakers often follow a healthy convention of detaching themselves from party politics to ensure that their rulings are perceived as completely impartial.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the independence of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha get structurally secured under the Indian Constitution?
opts: By making their salary and allowances subject to annual vote of the Parliament.
By charging their salary and allowances upon the Consolidated Fund of India, which is not subject to vote.
By prohibiting them from contesting parliamentary elections ever again.
By granting them executive powers over administrative ministries.
practiceQuestions.sol: The independence and impartiality of the Speaker are secured by several provisions, including charging their salary and allowances upon the Consolidated Fund of India (meaning they are not submitted to vote in Parliament), and protecting their work and conduct from discussion in the House except on a substantive motion.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional significance of the Speaker's power relating to Parliamentary Committees?
opts: The Speaker personally audits the accounts examined by the Public Accounts Committee.
The Speaker nominates all members and chairpersons of Parliamentary Committees of the Lok Sabha and guides their functioning.
The Speaker writes the final report for every parliamentary committee.
The Speaker holds veto power over recommendations made by the Estimates Committee.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha appoints/nominates chairpersons to all the parliamentary committees of the Lok Sabha and exercises administrative control over them. If any question of procedure arises in a committee, it is referred to the Speaker whose decision is final.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the position of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha compare with the Speaker of the House of Commons in the UK in terms of tenure continuity?
opts: In India, the Speaker vacates office immediately when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, whereas in the UK, once a Speaker, always a Speaker ('speaker once, speaker always').
In India, the Speaker serves a fixed tenure of 5 years regardless of House dissolution, unlike the UK.
There is no difference; both are automatically re-elected for life.
The UK Speaker is appointed by the monarch, whereas the Indian Speaker is appointed by the Prime Minister.
practiceQuestions.sol: In the UK, following the convention 'once a Speaker, always a Speaker', the incumbent Speaker is virtually unopposed in general elections. In contrast, in India, the Speaker ceases to hold office immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Lok Sabha, though they remain in office until then, and they must contest general elections as a party candidate.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the unique constitutional position of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha concerning the casting vote versus the Speaker?
opts: The Chairman can vote in the first instance, whereas the Speaker cannot.
Both exercise a casting vote only when there is a tie, but the Chairman does so despite not being a member of the House.
The Chairman has a veto power over all legislation, which the Speaker lacks.
The Chairman can never exercise a casting vote under any circumstance.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha exercise a casting vote only in the case of a tie (equality of votes). However, the fundamental distinction is that the Speaker is an elected member of the Lok Sabha, whereas the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) is an external constitutional functionary who is not a member of the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule), judicial review applies to the decisions of the Presiding Officer. Which landmark Supreme Court judgment established this principle?
opts: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997)
S. R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)
practiceQuestions.sol: In the landmark Kihoto Hollohan case (1992), the Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of the Tenth Schedule but struck down the provision (Paragraph 7) that barred judicial review. The Court held that the presiding officer, while deciding defection cases, acts as a tribunal, and their decision is subject to judicial review on grounds of mala fides, perversity, etc.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to the office of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha when the House is dissolved prematurely by the President?
opts: The Speaker vacates office immediately upon dissolution.
The Speaker continues in office until the newly elected Lok Sabha meets, except for the period when a Pro-Tem Speaker takes charge.
The Speaker automatically becomes the President of India.
The Speaker is replaced by the Chief Justice of India until elections.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike other members of the Lok Sabha whose membership ends with the dissolution of the House, the Speaker does not vacate their office upon dissolution. The Speaker continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Lok Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Speaker's power to certify a Money Bill considered a vital instrument of institutional checks and balances?
opts: It allows the Rajya Sabha to amend tax proposals freely.
It prevents the unelected/indirectly elected Upper House from blocking or altering financial measures passed by the directly elected representative House.
It gives the President absolute veto over budget allocations.
It allows the judiciary to rewrite fiscal policies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha has very limited powers over them (it cannot reject or amend them, only make recommendations within 14 days). By vesting the sole certification power in the Speaker, the Constitution ensures that the democratic will of the directly elected Lok Sabha prevails in financial matters.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of parliamentary democracy in India, what is the significance of the Panel of Chairpersons for the Lok Sabha?
opts: They exercise all powers of the Speaker permanently when the Speaker is on foreign tours.
They are nominated by the Speaker to preside over the House in the absence of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker.
They are elected by a special majority of the Rajya Sabha to oversee Lok Sabha bills.
They have the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha independently.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the rules of Lok Sabha, the Speaker nominates a panel of not more than ten chairpersons from among the members. Any of them can preside over the House in the absence of the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker. However, a member of the panel cannot preside when the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker is vacant.

practiceQuestions.q: How are the salaries and allowances of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha determined?
opts: By presidential ordinance issued every fiscal year.
By Parliament by law, as specified under Article 97 of the Constitution.
By recommendations of the NITI Aayog without parliamentary approval.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 97 of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be paid to the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States and to the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People such salaries and allowances as may be fixed by Parliament by law.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The election of the Speaker is conducted by the Election Commission of India.
2. The date of election of the Speaker is fixed by the President of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Parliament and state legislatures, but the election of the Speaker is an internal affair of the House conducted among its members, presided over by the Pro-Tem Speaker. Statement 2 is correct: The date of election of the Speaker is fixed by the President of India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker decides whether a particular matter attracts the anti-defection law.
2. The decision of the Speaker under the anti-defection law is final and immune from judicial review under all circumstances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Under the Tenth Schedule, the presiding officer of the House is empowered to decide questions of disqualification on the ground of defection. Statement 2 is incorrect: While the law states the decision is final, the Supreme Court in the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992) ruled that the presiding officer's decision is subject to judicial review.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Chairman is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
2. The Chairman can be removed from office by a resolution passed in the Rajya Sabha by a special majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Vice-President (Chairman of Rajya Sabha) is elected by an electoral college consisting of both elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament (not just elected members). Statement 2 is incorrect: To remove the Vice-President, a resolution must be passed by the Rajya Sabha by an effective majority (a majority of all the then members of the house) and agreed to by the Lok Sabha by a simple majority; however, note that the removal is initiated in the Rajya Sabha, but the majority required in Rajya Sabha is an effective majority, not necessarily a 'special majority' as defined under Article 368, and the Lok Sabha needs only to agree by a simple majority.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The office of the Deputy Speaker is a constitutional office specifically created under Article 93 of the Constitution.
2. The Deputy Speaker is subordinate to the Speaker and is subject to the Speaker's administrative control.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 93 mandates that the Lok Sabha shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Furthermore, the Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker; they are independently elected by the House. However, in terms of presiding over the House when occupying the chair, they exercise identical powers, and the Deputy Speaker functions autonomously rather than as an agent of the Speaker, though administratively the Speaker heads the Lok Sabha Secretariat.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the certification of Money Bills:
1. The Speaker's certificate on a Money Bill is final and open to judicial review on substantive grounds.
2. If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the matter is referred to the President of India for final arbitration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 110(4) states the Speaker's endorsement is final, and although recent constitutional debates (such as Aadhaar Act routing) brought judicial scrutiny on whether bypassing the Rajya Sabha was constitutional, the literal text gives finality, and courts have debated the extent of review. More importantly, Statement 2 is completely wrong because the Constitution explicitly vests the sole authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill in the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, not the President.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. A resolution for removal of the Speaker can be moved only after giving at least 14 days' advance notice.
2. When a resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration, the Speaker can preside over the sitting of the House during that specific discussion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 94 requires a 14-day advance notice for moving a resolution to remove the Speaker. Statement 2 is incorrect: Under Article 96, when a resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration, the Speaker cannot preside at the sitting of the House, though they have the right to speak and take part in its proceedings and vote in the first instance (not casting vote).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pro-Tem Speaker:
1. The appointment and oath of the Pro-Tem Speaker are administered by the Chief Justice of India.
2. The office of the Pro-Tem Speaker is an explicit constitutional post detailed under Article 94 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because the Pro-Tem Speaker is appointed and sworn in by the President of India (not the Chief Justice of India, though sometimes the President appoints a senior judge to administer oaths to MPs, the Pro-Tem Speaker themselves is appointed by the President). Statement 2 is incorrect because the office of the Pro-Tem Speaker is not mentioned anywhere in the Constitution; it is an office created by parliamentary convention and practice.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Presiding Officers during a Joint Sitting of Parliament:
1. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting, and in their absence, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha takes the chair.
2. The rules of procedure of a joint sitting are compiled by the Rajya Sabha and approved by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha never presides over a joint sitting; if the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides, and if the Deputy Speaker is absent, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides. Statement 2 is incorrect because under Article 118(3), the President, after consultation with the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, makes rules as to the procedure with respect to joint sittings, not the Rajya Sabha alone.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the comparative powers of the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman:
1. Both officers have the final authority to permit or disallow an adjournment motion in their respective houses.
2. Both officers can vote in the first instance during regular legislative bills in their respective houses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is incorrect because an adjournment motion (which is an extraordinary device to draw attention to a matter of urgent public importance) can only be moved in the Lok Sabha, not in the Rajya Sabha. Therefore, the Rajya Sabha Chairman has no such power. Statement 2 is incorrect because neither the Speaker nor the Chairman can vote in the first instance; both only exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes, and furthermore, the Chairman is not even a member of the House.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker is ranked 7th in the Table of Precedence of the Republic of India, along with the Chief Justice of India.
2. The Speaker cannot be removed from office under any circumstances without the explicit concurrence of the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: In the Indian Table of Precedence, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is placed at rank 7, alongside the Chief Justice of India. Statement 2 is incorrect: The removal of the Speaker is an internal parliamentary process decided solely by a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by an absolute majority. The Prime Minister's concurrence is not constitutionally required for the removal of the Speaker.
